chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a female slave as a mut'ah (temporary marriage) in addition to a free woman. He said: No. The correct view is to consider that it is not permissible for him to marry her except with the permission of the free woman, as we have clarified in the narration of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', without that being forbidden in all cases.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying a female slave as a temporary wife while having a free wife?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on a man marrying a female slave in temporary marriage (*mutah*) while already married to a free woman. The Imam resolves the apparent permissibility by linking it to the precedent of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', establishing that the free wife's consent is a necessary condition for validity rather than an absolute prohibition if withheld. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of reconciling textual permissibility with practical conditions derived from companion reports.
